obligations.note: release now returns the stored confirmation only when the prior release is less than one day old; after that it calls _send_disbursement and add_release again for the same instruction_id. That is a second disbursement, and the passing test_sampled_release_is_idempotent is only sample coverage, so it does not satisfy the exhaustive requirement. No approved exception covers PAY-2.
CHG-26088 is approved by change manager Erik Brandt before review, and its components list payments.payments, which is the component for the only changed path, payments.py.
Sofia Santos, a payments change_approver and not the author Mara Costa, approved a code_review of commit cfa8da2f7bd2fe936a37d713fb11faa2072ec4a1.
The change is a single commit and the code_review approval names that same head commit.

records/ci/run.json records a successful payments suite on the head commit, and the JUnit report shows 172 tests, 0 failures, and 0 skipped, including the registered PAY-2 control test test_sampled_release_is_idempotent.
The only touched component, payments.payments, is not marked security_sensitive, so a security_review approval is not required.
payments.py is outside the protected paths (controls data, control tests, and CI), so a control_owner approval is not required.
The ticket type is standard and the change record sets emergency to false, so a post-implementation review is not due.

The release-window change is a deviation from PAY-2, and the register has no approved, unexpired exception scoped to PAY-2 and payments.payments. EXC-0141 is expired and covers SES-1, not this deviation.

ACR-0403 covered payments.py release and lapses because that behavior changed. The head-commit CI run re-executed the registered sample control test for PAY-2, which matches the sample strength of the lapsed trace.

summary: The change alters payments payment release so a replayed instruction is reused only for one day and is sent again after that. That violates PAY-2, which requires that the same payment instruction never produce a second disbursement, and there is no valid exception. Change-ticket, independent approval, commit coverage, CI, and the inapplicable security, control-owner, and emergency conditions are in order, but the unexcused double-disbursement path blocks acceptance.
